narrative.abstract: This report should be read as a strategic mathematical note rather than as a project-management checklist. Its purpose is to explain why the current route does not yet close the main conjecture, what theorem package is still missing, and which nearby routes remain mathematically meaningful.
narrative.bottleneck: The decisive bottleneck is the leading magnification bridge. The final reduction from the nonuniform target to the main conjecture is already available, so the strategic question is whether the bridge object can be fixed and the source-realization, transport, route, and payoff lemmas can be discharged.
narrative.subresult_value: Several missing items would already count as mathematically meaningful subresults even if the main conjecture remained open, especially a clean source-to-object realization theorem, a transport theorem for the invariant, or a barrier result ruling out one of the operationalizations.

summary_answer.headline: The proof is not blocked at the final reduction to P versus NP; it is blocked at the leading magnification bridge.
summary_answer.detail: To complete the proof on the current macro-strategy, one must fix a single bridge operationalization and then prove the source-realization, invariant-transport, route, and payoff lemmas that yield `NP not in P/poly`. Once that theorem is in hand, the final implication to `P != NP` is already available in the KB.

main_conjecture.title: P versus NP
main_conjecture.grounding_implication: If NP is not contained in P/poly, then P != NP.
main_conjecture.narrative: The current macro-proof does not try to prove P != NP directly. It organizes the search around a stronger nonuniform separation claim, then grounds the main conjecture by the implication NP not in P/poly implies P != NP.
